newsitem.title: USA: Honeywell motion in patent dispute denied.
newsitem.headline: Honeywell motion in patent dispute denied.

text.p: Honeywell Inc Friday said a federal judge denied the company's petition for a rehearing in a patent dispute with Litton Industries Inc.
In a statement, the company said the September 11 ruling was issued by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.

In a separate ruling on September 9, the company said the the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California ordered the parties to mediate the patent and antitrust claims before retired California Supreme Court Chief Justice Malcolm Lucas, a process that the company said has begun.
In July, a federal appeals court upheld a jury verdict in favor of Litton Industries in a patent infringement suit against Honeywell and ordered a new trial to determine damages.

Honeywell disputes the ruling on the patent and has vowed to appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court. Meanwhile, it said it would continue its preparation for any new damages trial and to oppose any injunctive relief which Litton might seek, in the event the appeal is unsuccessful or the mediation does not lead to a settlement of the cases.
Originally, a jury awarded Litton $1.2 billion in the suit, which centered on whether Honeywell infringed a patent for a laser gyroscope navigation and guidance system.

The jury verdict was overturned in January 1995 by a judge who ruled the Litton patent was invalid. In July, the appeals court reversed that decision and ordered the case returned to the judge to determine damages.
In the antitrust dispute, a jury ordered Honeywell to pay Litton $702 million in damages but a judge ordered a new trial on the damages after ruling that Litton's damage study was flawed.
